I tested publishing the county's 2.4M parcel polygons as a hosted feature layer in ArcGIS Online vs. serving them as vector tiles from our PostGIS database via pg_tileserv. Vector tiles loaded the full county at zoom 12 in about 1.8 seconds versus 9 seconds for the hosted feature layer, but the hosted layer supports the editing the client wants. I recommend a hybrid: hosted layer for editing, vector tile layer refreshed nightly for the public map, and I need her decision by Friday noon.
tasks.draft:
Subject: Update on Parcel Data Proof-of-Concept

Hi Priya,

I hope you're having a great week! I wanted to take a moment to reach out and share a quick update on the parcel data proof-of-concept that we discussed earlier. I've now had the chance to complete the initial round of testing, and I'm happy to share some of the key findings with you.

To evaluate the two approaches, I tested publishing the county's 2.4M parcel polygons as a hosted feature layer in ArcGIS Online, as well as serving them as vector tiles from our PostGIS database using pg_tileserv. In terms of performance, the vector tiles loaded the full county at zoom 12 in about 1.8 seconds, whereas the hosted feature layer took about 9 seconds. However, it's worth noting that the hosted layer supports the editing capabilities that the client is looking for, which is an important consideration.

Based on these results, I would recommend a hybrid approach. This would involve using the hosted layer for editing, and a vector tile layer that is refreshed nightly for the public map. This would give us the best of both worlds in terms of performance and functionality.

If possible, I would really appreciate getting your decision by Friday noon so that we can move forward in time for the client update.

Please let me know if you have any questions or if you would like to discuss further. Thanks so much for your time, and I look forward to getting your decision by Friday noon!

Best,
[Name]

tasks.draft:
Subject: Proposal: Extracting the Payments Module into a Standalone Service

Hi Priya,

I hope you're having a great week so far! I wanted to take a moment to reach out and share some thoughts on an architectural topic that I believe is worth our attention as we head into planning for the new year.

After careful consideration, I would like to recommend that we split the payments module out of our monolith and into its own dedicated service, with work starting in Q1. I believe this change could offer meaningful benefits for both our reliability and our delivery speed.

To give you some context, our monolith currently deploys on a weekly cadence, and as a result, payments changes are blocked by the release train roughly 40% of the time. In addition, payments handles around 12,000 requests per minute at peak, and it was responsible for two of last quarter's three Sev-1 incidents. Taken together, these factors suggest that the current setup is holding us back.

In terms of effort, we estimate that the work would require two engineers for approximately 10 weeks, which I believe is a reasonable investment given the potential upside.

I would really appreciate your approval on this at Thursday's architecture review. Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss any of this in more detail beforehand.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration, and I look forward to hearing your thoughts!

Best regards,
[Your Name]
